name: Get a winter's firewood
summary: Start now: split hardwood takes one to two years to dry and softwood about a summer, so wood cut this winter is next winter's heat. In town, take fallen trees and storm blowdown first, then sawmill slabs and offcuts, plain lumberyard boards, bare solid-wood furniture and pallets stamped HT (heat-treated); leave anything painted, treated, glued or stamped MB or SF. A bow saw, axe, maul and wedges need no fuel; a chainsaw is faster and far more dangerous. Split it, stack it off the ground and cover the top as soon as it's home.

parts.why: The fuel: fallen trees, sawmill offcuts, plain boards, bare solid wood and HT pallets
Roofing over the top of the stack; leave the sides open
Petrol for a chainsaw, mixed with two-stroke oil as its maker says
Bar and chain oil for a chainsaw

tips: Drying sets the calendar: split softwood dries in about a summer, hardwood in one to two years (Drolet Part 1, CMHC wood heat).

A medium-sized house heated only with wood needs about 2 to 5 full cords a winter (NRCan says 3 to 5, CMHC 2 to 4); 1 to 2 with an efficient stove in the main room, or when the stove does part of the job. Those are whole-house figures, and only experience tells (NRCan wood heating, CMHC wood heat).
Fallen wood first. Keep two tree lengths from a dead standing tree you aren't felling (OSHA eTool hazards).
Never cut a tree with a wire in it or touching it. Stay 10 m (33 ft) back and treat the line as live (BC Hydro, OSHA trim).
Sawmills keep slabs, cut-offs and cull logs (CMHC wood heat). At lumberyards take plain untreated boards only.
Never burn pressure-treated wood, railway ties, plywood, particle board or anything glued (Drolet Part 1, EPA Burn Wise, EPA CCA).

Pallet stamps name the treatment: HT is heat treatment to at least 56 °C through the wood for 30 minutes; MB (methyl bromide) and SF (sulphuryl fluoride) are chemical fumigations (CFIA D-98-08, CFIA wood packaging).

Never burn pallets stamped MB (Penn State pallets), painted ones, or any that look stained or contaminated (Chugach officials). We leave SF ones too, as our own caution. An unstamped pallet tells you nothing about what it carried.

Furniture: bare solid wood only, nothing painted or coated (EPA Burn Wise). Paint on older pieces may hold lead: Health Canada warns that heat guns and blowlamps on lead paint make toxic dust and fumes, and we treat burning it the same way (Health Canada lead paint).
Pull every nail, staple and screw out of pallet and furniture wood before a saw touches it: look for nails, spikes and other metal before every cut (OSHA chainsaws).
Chainsaw work: never alone, and wear leg protection, a hard hat, eye and face protection, hearing protection, gloves and protective boots (OSHA chainsaws).
A bow saw or crosscut saw, an axe, a splitting maul and two steel wedges keep working when the petrol runs out.
Burn wood near where it was cut: moving it spreads tree pests, and moving firewood out of a CFIA regulated area is prohibited (CFIA firewood).
